title: Sulfur- and phosphorus-standardized metal quantification of biological specimens using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
protocol: Prepare cells the day before they will be needed.
Change media when cells reach approximately 80% confluency or desired level.
Replace media with media containing vehicle or drug of interest for a treatment duration of 24 hours.
Use 300 μM copper(II) chloride in SH-SY5Y cells for the experiment.
For HAP1 cells, use 400 μM copper(II) chloride and 400 μM BCS.
Select drug concentrations based on cell type and experimental goals.
Determine IC50 for copper using colorimetric or fluorescence assays if testing potentially toxic metal doses.
Treat primary cultured fibroblasts with 50 μM copper without causing overt toxicity.
Recommend treating cells with a range of 50–400 μM copper(II) chloride.
Change media the day before freezing cell samples if not using drug treatment.
Detach cells using PBS-Trypsin or PBS-EDTA depending on the cell type and experiment requirements.
Warm PBS and PBS-Trypsin to 37°C if using trypsin.
Place additional PBS on ice.
Wash cells once with 10 mL of warm PBS.
Add 3 mL of PBS-Trypsin and incubate for 2 min at 37°C until cells begin to detach.
Detach cells from the plate with gentle aspiration using a pipette.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL tube and dilute with 6 mL of warm PBS.
For blank controls, add 3 mL of PBS with trypsin and 6 mL of PBS to the corresponding 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 130 × g (800 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C to pellet the cells.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend in 5 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Mix well and add 1 mL of your cell suspension to each microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 210 × g (1,500 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C to pellet the cells.
Remove supernatant.
Immediately transfer tubes to dry ice to snap freeze your samples.
Leave samples on dry ice for 15–30 min.
Transfer to −80°C for long-term storage.
Wash each plate twice with 10 mL ice-cold PBS.
Add 10 mL PBS-EDTA to each plate and place on ice for 10 min.
Detach cells from the plate with gentle aspiration using a pipette.
Place the suspension in a 15 mL tube.
For blank controls, add 10 mL of PBS-EDTA to a tube.
Centrifuge at 130 × g (800 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C to pellet the cells.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of ice-cold PBS.
Transfer to labeled screw cap tubes.
Centrifuge this cell suspension at 210 × g (1,500 rpm) for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant carefully to remove as much PBS as possible.
Immediately transfer tubes to dry ice to snap freeze your samples.
Leave samples on dry ice for 15–30 min before transferring to −80°C for long-term storage.
Mix well after transferring the cell suspension to a 15 mL tube.
Count the cells in the mixed suspension.
Calculate the volume of PBS needed based on the desired cell number per tube.
Resuspend counted cells in approximately half of the cold PBS required for the final concentration.
Count cells again after resuspending in cold PBS.
Dilute the cell solution with cold PBS to achieve the desired cell concentration.
Mix well the diluted cell suspension.
Add 1 mL of the cell suspension to each microcentrifuge tube.
Resuspend SH-SY5Y cells to a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Prepare samples containing 1 × 10^6, 2 × 10^6, or 3 × 10^6 cells (0.5 mL, 1 mL, or 1.5 mL per tube).
Dilute remaining cells by a factor of 4 in PBS to achieve a concentration of 500,000 cells/mL.
Prepare samples containing 250,000 or 500,000 cells (0.5 mL or 1 mL per tube).
Collect D. melanogaster larvae from each genotype.
Wash collected larvae in PBS to remove food particles.
Place small puddles of 1× PBS in each of two SYLGARD™-filled petri dishes or empty petri dishes for rinsing larvae.
Weigh and freeze all the larvae for one genotype after collection and washing.
Rinse both petri dishes with fresh PBS before collecting larvae from an additional genotype.
Use forceps to collect 3-5 wandering third-instar female larvae from the vial.
Place the collected larvae in a pool of 1× PBS in one petri dish.
Under a dissecting microscope, select and remove male larvae by distinguishing them based on gonads under the cuticle in the posterior ventral segment.
Lightly grasp an individual larva with forceps and gently jostle it side-to-side within the PBS to remove food residue.
If necessary, use one forceps tip to gently brush along the larval body to dislodge remaining food residue.
Move the cleaned female larvae to a pool of PBS in a second petri dish.
Repeat steps 24 and 25 using a third petri dish if food particles are visible in the second petri dish.
Clean the petri dish used initially, add fresh PBS, and repeat steps 23-25 for additional larvae as needed.
Individually weigh each larva after all animals of a single genotype have been collected.
Freeze each weighed larva.
Use forceps to remove an individual larva from the petri dish.
Place the larva on a Kimwipe to remove PBS.
Pick up the larva using forceps and place it gently in a microcentrifuge tube.
Screw on the cap of the microcentrifuge tube and label the tube.
Prepare empty microcentrifuge tubes for blank controls.
Determine the baseline weight of the microcentrifuge tube and screw cap using an analytical balance.
Record the baseline value.
Reweigh the microcentrifuge tube with the larva and cap, then record this value.
Subtract the baseline value from the post-weight to determine the larva's weight.
Transfer the tube to dry ice to snap-freeze the larva.
Repeat steps 27–29 for each larva collected.
Assign larvae by weight to groups for analysis.
Place microcentrifuge tubes with individual larva on dry ice.
Combine all larvae for a given group in a single tube using forceps or gentle tapping.
Dislodge larvae stuck to the side of the tube before transferring.
Dissolve samples in 70% nitric acid.
Turn on heat block and set to 95°C.
Rinse a 25 mL or 50 mL tube with MilliQ water.
Add a small volume of 70% nitric acid (approximately 2 ml) to the tube.
Add 20 μL of 70% nitric acid to each sample using the repeating pipettor.
Briefly centrifuge to collect the nitric acid and the sample at the bottom of the tube if required.
Use nitric acid to dissolve samples, starting from a minimum volume of 20 μL.
Incubate samples in the heat block at 95°C for 10 min.
For high lipid content samples, follow incubation with equal volume of concentrated trace element grade hydrogen peroxide.
Dilute samples in 2% nitric acid for analysis immediately or store at room temperature for up to 3 months before dilution.
Dilute samples in 2% nitric acid by mixing 780 μl with 20 μl of sample.
Transfer diluted samples to a deep 96 well plate, ensuring minimum volume of 400 μl per well.
Alternatively, transfer undiluted samples directly into the deep 96 well plate and dilute in 2% nitric acid within the wells.
Seal the 96 well plate with sealing tape if storing for up to one month at room temperature; otherwise analyze immediately.
Operate the Thermo iCAP-TQ series inductively coupled plasma triple quadrupole mass spectrometer (ICP-MS) in oxygen reaction mode.
Filter for m/z ion at 31 and 32 which filters out Ti and Ca interference ions using the first quad.
React S+ and P+ with O2 in the octopole to shift their masses by one oxygen.
Detect 48SO+ & 47PO+ after the third quadrupole without polyatomic or ion Ca and Ti interference.
Prepare a nine-point external calibration curve to quantify iron (Fe), copper (Cu), manganese (Mn), cobalt (Co), and zinc (Zn).
Prepare 50 mL stock solutions of Multielement Calibration Standard for ICP-MS in 2% nitric acid.
Dilute the stock solutions to create a series ranging from 0.5 to 1,000 μg*L-1, increasing by 2× at each point (0, 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500 and 1,000 μg*L-1).
Dilute solutions using the 2DX prepFAST M5 system or through standard dilution practices manually.
Monitor for potential instrument drift by automatic dilution of the sample with the Internal Standard for ICP-MS during sample introduction.
Warm up and tune the ICP-MS instrument as recommended by the manufacturer.
Prepare a four-point standard curve for sulfur using dilutions of a 100 mg/L sulfur calibration standard in 2% nitric acid (0.5, 1, 5, 10 mg/L).
Set the r2 for calibration curves to > 0.9998.
Make up Seronorm Trace Elements Serum L-1 and L-2 standard reference material according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Replace any sealing tape previously added with X-Pierce Sealing Film for robotics.
Add samples and Seronorm Trace Elements Serum L-1 and L-2 to the sample deck.
Build the worklist.
Run the Seronorm Trace Elements Serum L-1 and L-2 (800 μL of a 1:40 dilution in 2% nitric acid).
Verify that the measurement of elements is within +/-20% of accepted values.
Continue with measurement of samples.
Intersperse a Seronorm measurement every 20–30 samples.
Conduct data analysis within the Qtegra software.
Export values from Qtegra.
